item.title: Investors flip the switch on the AI trade
item.itunes:title: Investors flip the switch on the AI trade
item.itunes:subtitle: After tech stocks tumbled, are markets entering a new era?
item.description:
With heavy losses on the Nasdaq and Anthropic’s sliding share price, markets are bracing for more volatility. High interest rates and the affordability crisis have effectively frozen the US real estate market, the world’s most important climate talks failed to reach an agreement, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will defend his “reset” deal with the EU in the face of criticism from three of his predecessors and immigrants’ income growth is outstripping Spaniards.


Mentioned in this podcast:

What happens when bubbles burst

The American dream of home ownership recedes as mortgage rates surge

COP31 climate talks fail after stand-off over fossil fuels

Burnham reopened the Brexit debate. He now sees the political dangers ahead

Andy Burnham seeks quick tuition fees deal with the EU

Burnham’s EU dreams hampered by ministers’ doubts

Immigrants’ income growth outstrips Spaniards’ under Pedro Sánchez

Credit: Reuters

item.title: Martin Wolf on the US midterms: Could history help predict the next two years of US politics?
item.itunes:title: Martin Wolf on the US midterms: Could history help predict the next two years of US politics?
item.itunes:subtitle: Historian Heather Cox Richardson on how Democrats should take the fight to Trump
item.description:
The Democrats swept the midterms. Donald Trump is still president. What will the next two years look like? And what can history teach us about what comes next? Martin Wolf speaks to historian Heather Cox Richardson about the cycles in the past 250 years of US politics — how renewal (and division) can both follow periods of oligarchy, and how the Democrats should react to a “constitutional crisis”.


To enjoy future episodes, be sure to subscribe to ‘Martin Wolf on the World’ wherever you get your podcasts. You can also watch Martin’s podcast series on the FT’s YouTube channel here: https://www.youtube.com/@FinancialTimes

item.title: Anthropic’s splashy public market debut
item.itunes:title: Anthropic’s splashy public market debut
item.itunes:subtitle: AI giant shares closed up 17% in its Wall Street debut
item.description:
Anthropic closed up 17% per cent in its Wall Street debut and Prime Minister Andy Burnham is trying to strike a deal to bring the UK closer to the EU. Plus, Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin for what he called a “groundbreaking” trilateral meeting.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Anthropic shares jump 17% after record Wall Street listing

France and UK at loggerheads over food rules ahead of key EU summit

Xi, Trump and Putin hail ‘groundbreaking’ meeting

item.title: Anthropic’s big IPO day arrives
item.itunes:title: Anthropic’s big IPO day arrives
item.itunes:subtitle: Frenzy for AI stock is testing how far Wall Street will go to accommodate a new army of individual investors
item.description:
Retail investors vying for a piece of Anthropic’s blockbuster listing are facing off against an avalanche of institutional demand, US President Donald Trump will meet Russia’s leader Vladimir Putin and China’s premier Xi Jinping today in Shenzhen, and investors are increasingly questioning gold’s traditional status as a haven asset in portfolios. Plus, Chris Miller, the author of “Chip War” explains why US Congress is pushing for stricter export controls for Nvidia’s most powerful chips.


Mentioned in this podcast:

How gold lost its lustre

Anthropic retail investors face squeeze in blockbuster IPO

What will Nvidia’s post-Huang era look like?

item.title: Nvidia board insists Huang won’t return as CEO
item.itunes:title: Nvidia board insists Huang won’t return as CEO
item.itunes:subtitle: Chip giant raises next year’s financial forecasts during earnings report as it doubled revenue last quarter
item.description:
Nvidia raised its sales forecast for next year after reporting strong earnings, as the $3.7tn chip designer at the heart of the AI boom insisted it would not bring back Jensen Huang as CEO, and Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos appears set to take over ECB presidency. Plus, Wall Street banks expect global corporate profit growth to slow sharply next year.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Nvidia insists Jensen Huang will not return as CEO as it reports strong sales

How Paris and Berlin sealed the ECB succession

Corporate earnings growth set to slow sharply next year as AI spending cools

AI asked ‘better questions’ than human accountants in pilot KPMG audit

item.title: Leak of 15mn Deutsche Bank files exposes systemic failures
item.itunes:title: Leak of 15mn Deutsche Bank files exposes systemic failures
item.itunes:subtitle: Email, internal probes and other documents throw new light on the career and leadership of chief executive Christian Sewing
item.description:
15mn leaked documents about Germany's Deutsche Bank show the lender failed to fix major problems over and over again. Nvidia’s board is not considering reinstating Jensen Huang as the company’s chief executive. Plus, a UK report on youth unemployment will call for a “complete system reset” of how the British state interacts with young people.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Nvidia board not considering reinstating Jensen Huang as chief executive
